# Nehemiah Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 471v–472r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When the wall had been built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites had been appointed,

**2** I gave my brother Hanani and Hananiah the commander of the fortress charge over Jerusalem, for he was a man of integrity and feared God more than many.

**3** I said to them, "Do not let the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun is hot. While the gatekeepers are still on duty, have them shut and bar the doors. Appoint guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his post and each in front of his own house."

**4** The city was spacious and large, but the people within it were few, and no houses had been rebuilt.

**5** Then my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people for registration by genealogy. I found the genealogical record of those who had first returned, and in it was written:

**6** These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.

**7** They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:

**8** the sons of Parosh, 2,172; **9** of Shephatiah, 372; **10** of Arah, 652; **11** of Pahath-moab (of Jeshua and Joab), 2,818; **12** of Elam, 1,254; **13** of Zattu, 845; **14** of Zaccai, 760; **15** of Binnui, 648; **16** of Bebai, 628; **17** of Azgad, 2,322; **18** of Adonikam, 667; **19** of Bigvai, 2,067; **20** of Adin, 655; **21** of Ater (of Hezekiah), 98; **22** of Hashum, 328; **23** of Bezai, 324; **24** of Hariph, 112; **25** of Gibeon, 95.

**26** The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, 188; **27** of Anathoth, 128; **28** of Beth-azmaveth, 42; **29** of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, 743; **30** of Ramah and Geba, 621; **31** of Michmas, 122; **32** of Bethel and Ai, 123; **33** of the other Nebo, 52; **34** of the other Elam, 1,254; **35** of Harim, 320; **36** of Jericho, 345; **37** of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, 721; **38** of Senaah, 3,930.

**39** The priests: of Jedaiah (of the house of Jeshua), 973; **40** of Immer, 1,052; **41** of Pashhur, 1,247; **42** of Harim, 1,017.

**43** The Levites: of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah, 74.

**44** The singers: of Asaph, 148.

**45** The gatekeepers: of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, 138.

**46** The temple servants: of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, **47** Keros, Sia, Padon, **48** Lebanah, Hagabah, Shalmai, **49** Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, **50** Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, **51** Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, **52** Besai, Meunim, Nephishesim, **53** Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, **54** Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, **55** Barkos, Sisera, Temah, **56** Neziah, and Hatipha.

**57** The sons of Solomon's servants: of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, **58** Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, **59** Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim, and Amon.

**60** All the temple servants and sons of Solomon's servants, 392.

**61** The following came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but could not prove their ancestral houses or their descent — whether they belonged to Israel:

**62** the sons of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 642.

**63** And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai — who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.

**64** These searched for their entries among those enrolled in the genealogies, but they were not found. So they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.

**65** The governor told them not to eat of the most holy food until a priest could minister with Urim and Thummim.

**66** The whole assembly together was 42,360,

**67** besides their 7,337 male and female servants. They also had 245 male and female singers.

**68** Their horses, 736; their mules, 245;

**69** their camels, 435; their donkeys, 6,720.

**70** Some of the heads of fathers' houses gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury: 1,000 gold drachmas, 50 basins, and 530 priestly garments.

**71** Some heads of fathers' houses gave into the treasury of the work: 20,000 gold drachmas and 2,200 silver minas.

**72** What the rest of the people gave: 20,000 gold drachmas, 2,000 silver minas, and 67 priestly garments.

**73** The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns. When the seventh month came, the people of Israel were in their towns.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Nehemiah 7 serves as a transitional chapter bridging the physical reconstruction of the wall (chs. 1-6) with the spiritual and communal reconstruction that follows (chs. 8-13). The census list, largely parallel to Ezra 2, is not redundant but serves a distinct purpose: in Ezra it records who returned, while in Nehemiah it records who belongs. The notation that the city was large but nearly empty (v. 4) is the chapter's narrative engine — walls require inhabitants, and the community must know itself before it can be whole. The exclusion of priests who cannot verify their genealogy (vv. 63-65) and the appeal to Urim and Thummim demonstrate a community that takes holiness boundaries seriously, even at the cost of administrative convenience.

---

## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "faithful man" vs. "man of integrity" vs. "man of exceptional integrity"
- **EMET:** "faithful man" (*ish emet*) / **LOGOS:** "faithful man" / **PNEUMA:** "man of exceptional integrity"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "man of integrity" — Hebrew *ish emet* literally means "man of truth/faithfulness." "Integrity" captures the breadth of *emet*. PNEUMA's "exceptional" is an unnecessary intensifier not in the text.

### V.4 — "no houses had been rebuilt" vs. "most of the houses had not yet been rebuilt"
- **EMET:** "no houses were-built" / **LOGOS:** "no houses had been rebuilt" / **PNEUMA:** "most of the houses had not yet been rebuilt"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "no houses had been rebuilt" — The Hebrew *eyn banuy* states absolutely "none were built." PNEUMA softens this beyond what the text warrants.

---

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
